title: Alabama Sales Tax: Rates, SSUT, and Compliance Guide
summary: Alabama sales tax ranges from 4% to 12%. See city rates, the 2% grocery rate, the flat 8% SSUT option for remote sellers, and what’s taxable.
body_markdown:
## Alabama sales tax at a glance


**State taxing authority** Alabama Department of Revenue


**Alabama sales tax rate** 4%


**Local sales tax rates** 0% to 8%


**Combined sales tax rate range** 4% to 12%


**Economic nexus threshold** More than $250,000 in total retail sales into Alabama in the previous calendar year (taxable and nontaxable)


**Website**[revenue.alabama.gov](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/)


**Tax line** 334-242-1490


Alabama’s state sales tax rate is 4%. Local rates range from 0% to 8%, so combined rates run from 4% to 12%, among the[highest in the country](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-by-state) .


Most tangible personal property is taxable, including computer software. Prescription drugs and most services are generally exempt. Groceries are taxed at a reduced 2% state rate, and local taxes may also apply.


Sellers with a physical presence in Alabama must register for a sales tax license. Out-of-state sellers with more than $250,000 in Alabama retail sales must register by Jan. 1 of the following year. Eligible remote sellers can use the Simplified Sellers Use Tax (SSUT) program to collect a flat 8%.


Businesses file and pay through[My Alabama Taxes](https://myalabamataxes.alabama.gov/) . Most businesses file monthly, and returns are due on the 20th of the following month. The state administers many city and county taxes, but not all. Check the local rate for each address.

## Alabama’s Simplified Sellers Use Tax program


Alabama has a unique[Simplified Sellers Use Tax (SSUT)](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/sales-use/simplified-sellers-use-tax-ssut/) program that allows remote sellers with nexus in Alabama to collect a flat 8% sales tax on eligible transactions in the state. This is designed to simplify collecting, filing, and remitting sales taxes for out-of-state sellers.


Alabama has separate state, county, and municipal sales taxes, and rates can vary significantly by address. Some local tax jurisdictions are self-administered, while others are administered by the state. This was very difficult for out-of-state sellers to navigate. Alabama launched SSUT in 2015 to solve this problem.


Remote sellers are eligible for SSUT if they sell tangible personal property or taxable services in Alabama from a location outside the state. They must not have a physical presence in Alabama or be otherwise required to collect standard in-state sales taxes.


Eligible sellers must apply for an SSUT account through[My Alabama Taxes](https://myalabamataxes.alabama.gov/) and receive approval before collecting the 8% sales tax rate.


Marketplace facilitators with $250,000 or more in Alabama sales generally must either register with ALDOR to collect and remit SSUT or comply with reporting and customer notification requirements.


If all your Alabama sales occur through a marketplace that collects and remits SSUT on your behalf, you do not need to register for an SSUT account or collect tax separately on those sales.


## Alabama sales tax rates and calculations


Alabama has a state-wide 4% sales tax rate. Cities, counties, and municipalities throughout Alabama have their own local sales tax rates, which range from 0% to 8%.


Some local taxes are state-administered, which means they’re processed through the Alabama Department of Revenue (ALDOR), while others are self-administered and processed by local governments.


### List of local sales tax rates in Alabama


Local sales tax rates in Alabama can vary significantly by city, ZIP code, and even by exact address. Use the[ALDOR’s rate lookup tool](https://www.alabamainteractive.org/ador_taxrate_lookup/welcome.action) to check sales tax rates by address before applying them to a sale.


Here are the sales tax rates in Alabama’s largest cities and towns.


City City rate County rate Combined rate


Auburn 4% 1% 9%


Birmingham 4% 2% 10%


Decatur 4% 1% 9%


Dothan 4% 1% 9%


Hoover 3.5% 2% (Jefferson County); 1% (Shelby County) 9.5% (Jefferson County); 8.5% (Shelby County)


Huntsville 4.5% 0.5% 9%


Madison 3.5% 1.5% (Madison County); 2% (Limestone County) 9% (Madison County); 9.5% (Limestone County)


Mobile 5% 1% 10%


Montgomery 3.5% 2.5% 10%


Tuscaloosa 3% 3% 10%


### How to calculate Alabama sales tax


To calculate Alabama sales tax, combine the state’s base rate of 4% with the local rates where the sale happens. Then, multiply the combined sales tax rate by the purchase price.


For example, if you’re selling an item for $50 in Birmingham, the total sales tax would be $5. That’s because Birmingham has a combined 10% sales tax rate, which includes 4% state tax, 2% county tax, and 4% city tax.


### Origin vs. destination sourcing in Alabama


For Alabama sales, the applicable local tax generally depends on where ownership of the goods transfers to the buyer.


- When a customer picks up an item at a store, the store’s location generally determines the rate.
- For delivered purchases, the delivery location generally determines the rate, but the seller must also consider its obligation to collect taxes in that local jurisdiction.


For example, if a retailer in Montgomery delivers a taxable item to a customer in Huntsville using its own truck, Huntsville’s combined 9% rate generally applies.


Making deliveries in its own truck establishes a physical presence that requires the retailer to collect the applicable local taxes.


Remote sellers outside of Alabama can apply for the SSUT program and use a flat rate of 8% for all taxable sales, regardless of the buyer’s location.


### Is Alabama a Streamlined Sales Tax state?


No. Alabama is not a Streamlined Sales Tax state. Sellers with nexus in Alabama must register directly through the state’s Department of Revenue.


## Sales tax nexus in Alabama


Nexus is the connection between a business and a state that requires it to file and remit sales taxes in that state.


There are four major types of sales tax nexus:


- **Physical:** The business has a physical presence in the state, such as an office, store, or warehouse. Numeral’s[physical nexus guide](https://www.numeral.com/blog/physical-nexus) provides more details.
- **Economic:** The business conducts a certain amount of economic activity in the state. Numeral’s[economic nexus guide](https://www.numeral.com/blog/economic-nexus) explains this further.
- **Affiliate:** The business has a legal connection with another company based in the state, such as a sister company.
- **Marketplace:** The business makes sales in the state through an online marketplace platform. Numeral’s[marketplace facilitator guide](https://www.numeral.com/blog/marketplace-facilitator) provides more information.


Here are the specific[sales tax nexus thresholds for Alabama](https://www.numeral.com/nexus/alabama) :


**Physical nexus** Any place of business in the state, including a retail store, office, warehouse, storage facility, or temporary sales booth, as well as any employees or inventory in the state


**Economic nexus**[More than $250,000 in total retail sales](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/ador-announces-sales-and-use-tax-guidance-for-online-sellers/) into Alabama in the previous calendar year (taxable and nontaxable)


**Affiliate nexus** A remote seller may establish affiliate nexus when it meets Alabama’s[related-party ownership tests](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/810-6-2-.90.01.pdf) with an in-state business and the businesses share branding, coordinate business plans, or conduct other qualifying activities supporting Alabama sales. Affiliate nexus generally prevents SSUT eligibility, although certain existing participants may remain in the program after acquiring an Alabama business. See Alabama Code Section 40-23-190.


**Marketplace nexus** Marketplace providers are required to file and remit sales taxes on behalf of their sellers.


## What’s taxable and exempt in Alabama


Most tangible personal property is subject to sales tax in Alabama, although several notable exemptions and reduced rates apply. However, most services are not subject to sales tax.


Here’s an overview of what is and isn’t taxable in Alabama:


Category Generally taxable? Notes


Tangible personal property Yes


Groceries Yes, with reduced rates Most food and grocery items are taxed at a reduced state rate of 2%, but local taxes may still apply.


Clothing Yes Eligible clothing items are exempt during the annual[back-to-school sales tax holiday](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/2026-Back-to-School-Sales-Tax-Holiday-Fact-Sheet.pdf) .


Prescription drugs No


SaaS Likely SaaS is not directly addressed by the state but is most likely taxable. See the SaaS section below.


Digital goods Varies Downloaded software is taxable under the software rule. Other digital products should be evaluated separately.


Services No


Shipping Varies This may be taxable if delivered by the seller or the shipping and handling is included in the price.


### What is subject to sales tax in Alabama


The following categories are generally subject to sales tax in Alabama:


- Tangible personal property
- Groceries (at reduced rate)
- Prepared foods
- Clothing
- Over-the-counter medication
- Computer software, including downloaded software, which is treated as tangible personal property, and SaaS
- Tickets to entertainment events


### What’s exempt from sales tax in Alabama


Here are the most notable sales tax exemptions in Alabama:


- Prescription drugs
- Most services
- Agricultural and farming items like seeds, livestock, or fertilizer
- Food stamp purchases
- Purchases made by government entities


### SaaS and digital goods taxability in Alabama


Alabama has no rule, ruling, or court decision that expressly addresses software as a service. However, Alabama[treats the licensing](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/810-6-1-.37-.pdf) of computer software as a retail sale subject to tax “regardless of its function or form of transmission.”


Because the licensing language may apply to a subscription to hosted software,[SaaS in Alabama is most likely taxable](https://www.numeral.com/blog/saas-sales-tax-alabama) .


Because this conclusion is an inference, not an explicit ruling, you should confirm the taxability of your specific product with ALDOR before collecting or relying on an exemption.


Separately stated charges for qualifying software programming and certain related services may be nontaxable. Other digital products should be evaluated separately; the software rule alone does not establish that every downloadable item is taxable.


### Resale and exemption certificates in Alabama


In Alabama, a[sales tax license](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/faq-categories/sales-tax-license/) also serves as a[resale certificate](https://www.numeral.com/blog/resale-certificates) . Properly licensed retailers can use it to purchase property intended for resale without paying sales tax.


Provide your sales tax license information to the vendor, who may request a copy of your license. Sellers must maintain records supporting the resale exemption, including the purchaser’s name, address, and sales tax account number.


Retailers located outside Alabama can use the sales tax license required by their home state to purchase property for resale tax-free. Alabama also accepts the[Multistate Tax Commission’s Uniform Sales & Use Tax Resale Certificate](https://www.mtc.gov/resources/uniform-sales-use-tax-exemption-certificate/) for qualifying resale purchases.


Qualifying businesses and organizations that are not required to hold an Alabama sales tax license may apply for a[Sales Tax Certificate of Exemption](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/faqs/how-do-i-obtain-a-certificate-of-exemption/) .


Use Form ST:EX-A1 for wholesalers, manufacturers, and other product-based exemptions, or Form ST:EX-A1-SE for statutorily exempt entities, and submit it according to the applicable instructions. These forms are not a general exemption available to every remote seller.


Exemption certificates are valid for one year and must be renewed annually. You may request renewal by email if the department has an application on file that is less than three years old and the information remains current. Otherwise, submit a new application.


Keep resale and exemption documentation with your sales tax records for at least the applicable assessment period, usually three years, but longer in some circumstances. Alabama’s recordkeeping rule generally measures that period from the return’s due date or payment date, whichever is later.


## Registering for an Alabama sales tax license


Businesses based in Alabama need a state sales tax license to[file and remit](https://www.numeral.com/product/filing-and-remittance) their sales taxes. Remote businesses that qualify for the Simplified Sellers Use Tax can apply for that program instead and do not need a sales tax license.


To get an Alabama sales tax license, apply through the[My Alabama Taxes (MAT) portal](https://myalabamataxes.alabama.gov/tap/_/) . See our[Alabama sales tax registration guide](https://www.numeral.com/sales-tax-registration/alabama) for detailed instructions.


You will need the following information about your business:


- Federal Employer Identification Number or Social Security Number
- Alabama Secretary of State Entity ID (if applicable)
- Legal business name, “doing business as” (DBA) name, and entity type
- NAICS code
- Your business’s physical address and mailing address
- The date you began (or plan to begin) making taxable sales in Alabama
- Contact information and addresses for all owners, partners, and officers


You will receive a confirmation number immediately after registering your business. However, it usually takes three to five business days to process your application.


After your application has been approved, you’ll receive your official account number, and ALDOR will mail you a copy of your sales tax license.


Registering for an Alabama sales tax license is free. Licenses must be renewed annually between Nov. 1 and Dec. 31, and you can renew online through MAT or, in some cases, via email.


Some municipalities in Alabama have self-administered local sales taxes. If you make sales in these municipalities, you may also need to register with the local government.


### Registration requirements for remote sellers


If you have economic sales tax[nexus in Alabama](https://www.numeral.com/nexus/alabama) , but do not have physical or affiliate nexus, you can register for the Simplified Sellers Use Tax (SSUT) program instead of registering for a standard Alabama sales tax license.


The process is very similar to registering for an in-state tax license. You’ll need to create an account through[My Alabama Taxes](https://myalabamataxes.alabama.gov/) and provide information about your business. When selecting the account type, you’ll need to choose “SSUT” instead of “Sales Tax”.


You must register by Jan. 1 of the next calendar year after meeting the economic nexus threshold of more than $250,000. Businesses can also voluntarily register and start remitting sales taxes before reaching economic nexus.


## Collecting Alabama sales tax


Once you’ve established sales tax nexus in Alabama, you’ll need to start collecting sales tax on eligible transactions.


Follow these steps to collect sales tax on each transaction:


1. Determine whether the item is taxable under Alabama law.
2. Determine the sourcing location. For in-person purchases, this is your store location. For online purchases, this is the buyer’s location.
3. Apply the correct combined sales tax rate, including state, county, and city taxes.
4. Collect the tax from the customer. Most point-of-sale and ecommerce platforms can collect sales tax automatically.
5. Track collected sales tax for future filing and reporting. Save receipts from each transaction for your records.


### Marketplace sales


In Alabama,[marketplace facilitators](https://www.numeral.com/blog/marketplace-facilitator) like Amazon, eBay, or Etsy are responsible for calculating, collecting, and remitting sales tax on behalf of their sellers. If you only sell to Alabama customers through a marketplace platform, you won’t be responsible for filing or remitting your own taxes.


If you sell online through both marketplace platforms and your own website, exclude sales made through an SSUT-participating marketplace that collects Alabama tax on your behalf when calculating Alabama’s economic sales tax nexus threshold. Include your direct retail sales, both taxable and nontaxable.


### Shipping and delivery charges


[Shipping and delivery charges](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/faqs/are-freight-charges-taxable/) are tax-exempt in Alabama if the item is delivered via USPS or another common carrier, are billed separately on the invoice, and are paid by the customer.


However, shipping charges may be taxable if the item is delivered by the seller’s vehicle and the charges are wrapped into the item price.


## Filing and paying Alabama sales tax


Businesses must file Alabama sales tax returns electronically through My Alabama Taxes (MAT).


To[file and remit](https://www.numeral.com/product/filing-and-remittance) , submit your return through MAT and pay any tax due. Payments of[$750 or more](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/sales-use/eft-threshold-of-750/) must be made electronically. For payments below $750, businesses can pay electronically or mail a check, but the return must still be filed online.


Some Alabama cities and counties have self-administered local sales taxes. Alabama businesses can file and remit taxes to these jurisdictions using the MAT[ONE SPOT system](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/sales-use/one-spot-filing/) , instead of using separate local systems.


Your Alabama sales tax filing frequency generally depends on your tax liability for the preceding calendar year. Most businesses are required to file monthly. You can request a different filing frequency as follows:


- **Quarterly:** if your tax liability is less than $2,400.
- **Semi-annual:** if your tax liability is less than $1,200, or you made sales in no more than two 30-consecutive-day periods during the preceding calendar year.
- **Annual:** if your tax liability is less than $600, or you made sales in no more than one 30-consecutive-day period during the preceding calendar year.


These reduced filing frequencies do not apply to the Simplified Sellers Use Tax program. SSUT sellers must file and pay each month electronically by the 20th of the following month.


Taxes are due by the 20th of the month following the reporting period. If the 20th falls on a weekend or a holiday, tax is due on the next business day.


For ACH debit payments through MAT, submit your payment information by 4 p.m. Central time on the due date. You must still file a return even if you had $0 in taxable sales during the reporting period.


For regular state sales tax, Alabama offers[discounts](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/faqs/is-the-seller-allowed-a-discount-for-timely-filing-and-paying-the-sales-tax-due/) for vendors who file and pay their taxes on time. The discount is 5% on the first $100 due, and 2% on all tax over $100. The total discount may not exceed $400 per month. Local taxes may have different discount rates even though they are filed through the ONE SPOT system.


SSUT participants receive a separate[discount](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/sales-use/simplified-sellers-use-tax-ssut/) of 2% on tax collected and remitted on time, capped at $8,000 per month.


### Filing Alabama sales tax online


Businesses file and pay sales tax through[My Alabama Taxes](https://myalabamataxes.alabama.gov/) (MAT), the state’s electronic portal. MAT handles state sales tax as well as city and county sales taxes.


[ONE SPOT](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/sales-use/one-spot-filing/) is the part of MAT that lets businesses file and pay state and local taxes in one place. You do not need to log in to each city or county site.


Numeral’s guide to filing[Alabama sales tax](https://www.numeral.com/blog/how-to-file-alabama-sales-tax-online) walks you through the process screen by screen.


## Alabama sales tax penalties and interest


ALDOR charges both[penalties](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/faqs/is-there-a-penalty-imposed-for-not-timely-filing-and-paying-the-sales-tax-due/) and interest for filing or remitting sales tax late. If you fail to file on time, the penalty is 10% of the tax due or $50, whichever is greater. If you fail to pay on time, the penalty is 10% of the tax due.


[Interest rates](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/legal/quarterly-interest-rates/) for late taxes in Alabama change each quarter. Interest rates for 2026 ranged from 6% to 7%.


## Alabama sales tax recordkeeping and audits


Alabama businesses should keep sales tax records for at least three years from the date the return was due or paid, and longer if[an audit](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-audit) or appeal is pending. These records include:


- Sales tax licenses
- Sales tax returns
- Receipts and invoices
- Bank statements
- Receipts for tax-exempt resale purchases


[Alabama may audit](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/legal/taxpayer-bill-of-rights/) businesses to make sure they collect, file, and remit sales tax correctly. If you disagree with a preliminary assessment, file a written[petition for review](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/legal/preliminary-assessment-appeal-rights/) with ALDOR within 30 calendar days of its issuance.


If ALDOR issues a final assessment, you can[appeal to the Alabama Tax Tribunal or circuit court](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/legal/final-assessment-appeal-rights/) within 60 days of its mailing or personal delivery, whichever occurs first. Follow the filing requirements for your chosen appeal route.

## Alabama sales tax FAQs


**What is the sales tax rate in Alabama?**
Alabama’s combined sales tax rate ranges from 4% to 12%, which consists of a 4% state tax rate and 0% to 8% in city, county, and municipal taxes.


**What is the economic nexus threshold in Alabama?**
The economic nexus threshold in Alabama is more than $250,000 in total retail sales into Alabama in the previous calendar year (taxable and nontaxable).


**Do marketplace sellers need to file sales tax returns in Alabama?**
No. If you’re only selling in Alabama via an online marketplace, the marketplace is responsible for collecting, filing, and remitting sales tax on your behalf.


**Are groceries and clothing taxable in Alabama?**
Yes. Groceries are taxed at a reduced state rate of 2%, and local taxes may also apply. Clothing is taxable, but eligible clothing is exempt during Alabama’s back-to-school sales tax holiday.
